facts.F1: In early 1998, the defendants, Mr. Lee Hoi-wing and Mr. Li Tung-ping, were negotiating to sell a large plot of land in the New Territories to Winghing Investments Limited.
facts.F2: The property was not owned by either Mr. Lee or Mr. Li, but by two Tsos, the Li Tak Kau Tso and the Li Tak Wo Tso.
facts.F3: The managers of the Tsos had passed away in the early 1940s, and Mr. Lee and Mr. Li were not in a position to sell the property.
facts.F4: Sales of land owned by a Tso required the consent of the government acting through the relevant District Office.
facts.F5: Winghing was also involved in negotiations for the purchase of three other properties from other vendors in the same area.
facts.F6: Mr. Lee informed Winghing that it would take around three to five years to obtain the necessary agreements from the members of the Tsos and the consent of the District Office.
facts.F7: The agreement for sale and purchase was signed on 15 June 1998, with a completion date dependent on the receipt of the District Office’s consent.
facts.F8: Winghing paid a further deposit of HK$744,192.80, taking the total deposit to 10% of the purchase price.
facts.F9: After the agreement was signed, Mr. Lee and Mr. Li obtained the necessary agreements from the members of the Tsos and lodged the applications with the Northern District Office.
facts.F10: The District Office’s consent was eventually obtained on 27 October 1999, and the defendants called on Winghing to complete the sale and purchase within 14 days.
facts.F11: Winghing failed to complete the sale and purchase and commenced proceedings against Mr. Lee and Mr. Li, claiming that the agreement had been validly terminated.
facts.F12: Winghing was aware of the formalities that needed to be completed before completion could take place, including the consent of the District Office.
facts.F13: Winghing had been offered the opportunity to include a cut-off date or long-stop date in the agreement to protect its position in the event of delays.
